module: LH-1 revision L pass 2: K2 machine with the exchange head
status: CAD and calculation only; nothing built or measured
frame: global deck frame; head at carriage centre xc, beam front face yf, z = local + 545

frame_geometry.X_beam: 100 x 50 x 5 6063-T6 rectangular tube on edge, 1167 mm: was 80 x 40 x 4 at 980
frame_geometry.deck_supports: 40 x 10 Al flat bars on edge at y [-351, -215, -105, 5, 115, 225, 336] (row boundaries + 5 mm, clear of the connector notches), on 2020 posts

envelope_mm.note: frame, enclosure panels, feet and drawer; the extraction fan behind the back panel adds 150 mm of depth

mass_kg.note: modelled solids at Al/steel/PC/PA12 densities; NOT included: deck modules (TC-1, shaker, thermal modules, balance, about 15 kg), fasteners, cables, electronics and supplies (about 15-20 kg): ESTIMATE

interference.method: bounding-box prefilter, OCC boolean common > 1 mm3; designed contacts excluded: tips/nozzles in the target place's labware, single-channel shafts in the target tube rack, the coupling halves meeting in a bay (balls/pins, stud/latch), the latch roller on the release-post ramp over its last 7 mm; Z sampled at 50, 85 and 100 % of each working stroke

z_clearance.tips_at_transit: lowest tip end at s 0 is z 190: tips clear every deck and shelf item; over the dock row tips are not allowed

dock_clearance.rule: a tool parked at the bottom of the stroke hangs 289 mm (Hn) below its plate; while one carriage works in a bay, the other carriage (tool up, NO TIPS) and the gripper pass over the neighbouring bays: their lowest points must clear the parked tools and the release posts by >= 8 mm
dock_clearance.consequence: pass 1 fails by about 90 mm: the other carriage's tool and the gripper fingers run into the neighbouring parked tools and posts.  Pass 2: Z stroke 345 and gantry +115 (beam mid z 545): nothing on the deck changes (same reach, same lowest fixed point z 190), the machine is 115 mm taller, the Z axes 115 mm longer, M1 grows (lever) and an exchange takes about 51 s instead of 26 s
planner_rules: no tips on EITHER carriage while the head is over the dock row (eject or park the idle carriage's tips first)
the dock row is entered and left at s 0 on all three axes; inside it only the exchanging carriage moves in Z

X.driving_targets: left: carriage B at bay 1 / gripper at column 1; right: gripper at the outer shelf column x 540, carriage A at bay 8
X.clearance_basis: swept head edge to the Y-carriage / rail-block inner faces (rev B rule)

Y.driving_targets: front: single channels at the front tubes of row F; back: the dock bays and the shelf slot behind G

total.note: a refill is two gripper moves (about 30 s together, rev K tip_supply timing); with the tip rules (p300 ~2,300) the p300 refills fall from 39 to 23

tip_waste.verdict_20L: FAILS the 1.5 x rule (it just covers 7,000 tips)
tip_waste.chosen: TB-2L: 500 x 340 x 170 mm lidded PP crate class (28.9 L gross) in the under-base drawer; the waste-canister bay moves right (bund wall at x 164)

tip_supply.basis: coordinator update (planner a418c41) sizing figures: 4,000 p300, 2,000 p200, 1,200 p10, 300 p1000; rule: largest need + 2 spare wafers of each type; towers capped at 150 mm above the shelf seat (MAX_LABWARE_H, as rev K)

spent_wafers.rule: the dedicated stack takes the first spent wafers; every tower slot that empties becomes a spent stack (planner rule), so one dedicated slot is enough

tip_supply.wafer_assumption: p300/p200/p10 wafer pitch 12/10/7 mm (rev K, ASSUMED); p1000 nested wafers at 20 mm pitch ASSUMED: if p1000 comes only in racks of 96, each rack takes a slot (5 slots)
what_it_would_take: 2 more slot(s): a third shelf column at x 670 needs the X carriage travel and the frame 130 mm wider (+130 mm of X beam: M1 beam torsion and bending terms grow about 12 % and 40 %)
or towers to 172 mm above the shelf (p300 10 wafers, p10 20): the head's lowest fixed point (z 190) then clears them by only 14 mm, under the 1.5 x clearance rule: not recommended
or size p300 for the tip-rule figure (about 2,300 + 2 spare wafers = 27 wafers, 4 towers) and keep the 4,000 figure for the no-rules case only: then the shelf fits with one slot to spare

plate_44mm_check.case: wash steps in a 96-well plate about 44 mm tall (0.5-2 mL deep-well class), then transfer to the 0.2 mL plate for thermal steps (coordinator: primary case)

square_2mL_44.basis: same rules as the 0.2 mL plate (rev K Y16): moved at 2 m/s2 = 2 mm + tilt rise; shaken = 6 mm freeboard

round_1.2mL_44.basis: same rules as the 0.2 mL plate (rev K Y16): moved at 2 m/s2 = 2 mm + tilt rise; shaken = 6 mm freeboard

gripper.grip_height: fingertips 2 mm above the seat on the full-height side wall: same as the 0.2 mL plate; the 113 mm fingers leave the gripper body 54 mm above the plate top
gripper.force: plate 0.06 kg + 96 x 2252 uL = 0.28 kg: needs about 5.4 N (mu 0.3 per pad, 2 m/s2, ASSUMED) within GR-1's 5-20 N; payload limit 0.6 kg: PASS
gripper.carried_clearance: carried at s 0 the plate bottom is at z 349: 9 mm over the release posts, 194 mm over the shelf towers: PASS

plate_44mm_check.lid: LD-1 (universal SBS lid, 9.5 mm, ceiling 1 mm above the rim) sits on the top frame if the deep-well plate has an SBS rim (most do; CONFIRM with the plate bought); lid top at z 51.5.  A deep-well plate is often sealed with a mat instead: the gripper cannot place a mat: stay with lids

magnet.MB-1: does NOT suit: MB-1 holds 2 mm magnets in rows between the 0.2 mL wells (5.4 mm cones at 9 mm pitch) with the magnet top 5 mm above the well floor; square 8.2 mm (or round 7 mm) deep wells leave 0.8-2 mm between wells: no room for the rows
magnet.needed: a bought 96 deep-well magnet plate (ring or bar magnets around/under each well, SBS footprint, about 20-25 mm tall, the plate sitting in it) on the standard place: B2 gets it as a swap insert (4 screws), or B4 holds it and the low-elution magnet moves to a C-row place
magnet.pellet: with the wash volumes the liquid stands 5.7 mm (200 uL) above the floor in the square well: the magnet must pull the pellet within the lowest 5 mm of the side wall (or to the floor ring) so beads are not lost high in the well; bench rig: bead capture at 200 uL and at the elution volume

shaker.clamp: the bought shaker clamps the SBS skirt (bottom 6-7 mm): deep-well plates share the footprint and skirt: PASS if the maker lists deep-well plates (CONFIRM); its maximum load and speed for a 0.2 kg plate (CONFIRM)
shaker.height: plate seat z 91: plate top 135, with lid 137.5: the head's lowest fixed point is z 190, so 52.5 mm in transit over D4: PASSES the 1.5 x clearance rule (<= 140) with the shaker sunk 40 mm (pass 2 fix)
shaker.what_it_takes: done in pass 2: shaker sunk 40 mm (unsunk it would top at z 177.5); otherwise recess the shaker about 40 mm (D4 is an edge place: a 150 x 108 cut-out in the deck and an under-deck frame at z -45; the shaker's own clamp stays above the deck) so the lidded deep-well plate tops at about z 140; or a lower bought heater-shaker class (about 80 mm body)

plate_44mm_check.weighing_nest: WN-1 (1 kg cell) takes a filled deep-well plate (0.28 kg) within its range; the K2 B1 entry already assumes this plate (44 mm): PASS
plate_44mm_check.stacking: the 51 mm stack cap (C4, D2: head rear parts behind deep work) takes ONE deep-well plate per place, not two: fresh deep-well plates need their own places or the shelf outer column (gripper only, no cap below 150: 3 per slot)
plate_44mm_check.cold_plate: CPB-1 (B3) is a block matched to the 0.2 mL wells: a deep-well plate does not seat in it.  Washes run at room temperature, so nothing is needed; a cold deep-well step would need a flat-bottom adapter block (custom, CPB-2)

what_must_change: a deep-well magnet plate (bought) for the wash steps; MB-1 stays for the 0.2 mL plate

the 0.5-10 uL eight-channel cannot reach the floor of a 44 mm plate with standard 10 uL tips (manifold hits the plate top): use the 5-50 uL tool for washes, or long 10 uL tips (about 45 mm, a fifth tip type)
